en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma while standing to those who were sitting. ...
[The Buddha said: “The training is to be observed: ‘I will not teach the Dhamma while standing to one who is sitting and not ill.
One who is standing must not teach the Dhamma to one who is sitting and not ill.”
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is standing while they are sitting and not ill, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it is unintentional … [and so forth] …
The tenth training rule is concluded.
